Connor Murphy’s ability to merge technical rigor with patient-centric design stood out during his time at VitalHealth Solutions. I’ll never forget the evening he spearheaded a critical overhaul of their provider scheduling API. Faced with a 40% latency spike during peak hours, he rearchitected the system using Python’s asynchronous capabilities, cutting response times by 62% within two weeks. His REST API design—prioritizing rate limiting and caching—reduced backend load by 35%, directly improving user experience for 12,000+ healthcare providers. This wasn’t just code; it was a systemic shift that balanced scalability with real-world impact.  

As a professor, I collaborated daily with Connor on prototyping tools for remote patient monitoring. His work ethic was unshakable—whether debugging complex MongoDB queries late at night or refining PostgreSQL indexing strategies to meet strict compliance deadlines. He thrived in our small agency’s fast-paced environment, often stepping into mentor roles for junior developers. His curiosity extended beyond code: he’d dissect AWS cost structures to optimize our infrastructure, and his Go-based microservices framework became a standard for new projects.  

Connor’s strength lies in his ability to translate abstract requirements into robust, scalable systems. His Python-driven analytics pipeline, which processed 500,000+ patient records daily, exemplifies this. He’s equally adept at navigating technical debt and rallying cross-functional teams.  

In short, Connor is a problem-solver who elevates both code and collaboration. I’m confident he’ll bring the same meticulousness and impact to any role.
